node.label: Patrick J. Geary
node.description: A medieval historian of relics, memory and ethnic identity. Furta Sacra (1978) studied thefts of relics in the central Middle Ages, and his essay ‘Sacred Commodities’ (1986) asks what made relics exchangeable within a particular medieval setting rather than assuming a timeless market. Phantoms of Remembrance (1994) concerns memory and oblivion at the end of the first millennium. The Myth of Nations (2002) uses research on changing early medieval identities to criticize modern nationalist claims to ancient continuity; Steven Fanning credits its central argument while warning that its survey contains questionable assertions and broad generalizations.
